transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. 

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise, heavy lifting, pilates, yoga, or swimming for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information! My next question is about my eye gel for dry eyes. When can I start using it again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using your eye drops or gel for dry eyes unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor. If you were using them before your operation, you can go ahead and use them again.

If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great to know, thanks! I'm also feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or if your eye is also red and painful along with the severe light sensitivity, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, got it. What about the blurriness—should I still have some by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details about how many days or weeks it's been since your operation. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about a week ago. Thank you for the information and your help with all my questions. I don't have any more questions at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! So just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery!
